summary: A vehicle versus pedestrian call brought an engine, a truck and a battalion chief to Almond Grove Lane.
A go-kart complaint came in from the Trentino neighborhood.
Officers were sent to a bar where a man with a knife in his pocket was reported threatening a customer.
An outside fire was reported at south Edison Road and David Road.
A medical aid call came in on Beale Avenue.

Deputies set a perimeter around an apartment complex and flew a drone over it after a suspect wanted on firearm and gang charges ran from a residence. Discarded clothing was found in a breezeway, patrol units were posted on the streets around the complex, and the search was called off a little after 8:30 p.m.

A tractor-trailer rig burned, with Engine 6 taking command and crews drawing tank water from a hydrant on the north side of the Brundage bridge. The trailer held nothing but produce, and a bystander was checked for possible smoke inhalation.
A transit bus went off the road at Belle Terrace and South Washington and six passengers reported pain; a third ambulance was started.
Two vehicles crashed on northbound Interstate 5 after another driver brake-checked traffic; the driver who caused it left before officers arrived and a no-contact hit-and-run report was taken.
A single gunshot was reported in the area of 22nd Street, with nothing else seen or heard.
A right-turn-only sign was knocked down at the dead end of East Belle Terrace at South Washington, and the city yard was asked to respond overnight.
A brush fire on Highway 33 drew a wildland response with two dozers, a helicopter, water tenders and several patrols.
Firefighters found smoke coming from the garage of a house on Delwood Avenue; the occupants were already out, the fire was knocked down and crews stayed for overhaul.
A grass fire about 10 feet by 20 feet was handled by a single engine.
A man who stole from a South Union business assaulted the person who confronted him, and a caller thought he had a weapon on him.
A caller reported hearing shots in the area; officers found people setting off aerial fireworks and cleared the call.
Deputies were sent to an address where three or four people were reported walking around with a shotgun.
Deputies went to a domestic disturbance on Starlight Peak Drive and found the subject on the back patio.
A reckless driving report came in from Elm Street west of Harrison in Ford City: high beams, high speed and no plate.

A grass fire on Elk Hills Road drew a wildland response with two dozers, a water tender and several patrols. Crews had to go in through oil field gates, and the company opened one for them. Battalion 2 kept three engines and the equipment on the fire and cancelled the rest of the response.
A missing person call was worked out of the city; the person was standing by with the reporting party.
A nude, intoxicated man was reported causing a disturbance on Linda Vista Drive.
Deputies were sent to an apartment complex where a man had threatened a resident and a roommate and then left with a handgun in a black backpack.

A man was shot in the head at a store on Highway 58 in Mojave and was unresponsive when deputies got there; they locked the business down. Witnesses reported a burgundy car with a disabled plate leaving, and two people ran toward nearby apartments.
An engine was sent to a carbon monoxide alarm on Teal Street.
Two men were reported fighting at a Union Avenue gas station.
A caller reported an impaired driver on Rosedale Highway at the north end of town.
A driver went the wrong way on Stockdale Highway and then southbound on Gosford Road. Officers lost sight of the car and reported that no unit was following it.
A person with traumatic injuries was found near South Chester Avenue and an ambulance was sent.
Multiple callers reported a fire in an apartment on Monterey Street and a rescue was started. The Red Cross was called in for three women and two men who were displaced.

Two vehicles crashed at Highway 119 and Tupman Road and both ended up in the roadway, one of them smoking with the driver still inside. The highway patrol was notified, the cars were pushed clear and both lanes were back open before 5 a.m.

A reinforced response went to a house fire on Angela Way in the Station 8 area. Crews found the house charged with smoke on the east side and fire showing at a rear corner, and a contents fire in the garage was knocked down with the gas and electric secured.
A vehicle burned fully involved out in a field near Mojave; no grass caught and the call went to the highway patrol.
A woman was reported yelling threats to kill someone and saying she had a firearm.
Infant reported not breathing at apartment near Planz Rd.
Person with cardiac arrest near Austin Street.
Vehicle collision with multiple injured people.
Deer injured in roadway and loaded into vehicle.
Man repeatedly trespassing and taking items.
Man in wheelchair rambling near Bakersfield.
Traffic stop on silver Lexus in Bakersfield.
